paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the LORD promises to restore His people. Right after the burning anger in Zephaniah 3:8, He says "For then…" (Zephaniah 3:9) and starts restoring. He gives pure lips so that all may call on His name, He removes the pride, and He leaves "a meek and humble people" who "will trust in the name of the LORD" (Zephaniah 3:12). That's the kind of God we're baking for.

And look at what He does for His people. He has "taken away your punishment" (Zephaniah 3:15), and He says "Do not fear, O Zion; do not let your hands fall limp" (Zephaniah 3:16). The reason is simple: "The LORD your God is among you; He is mighty to save" (Zephaniah 3:17). I think that's for the baker who's tired, worried or a little embarrassed about their past. The LORD doesn't just put up with His people, He is with them.

Then comes the part that gets me every time: "He will rejoice over you with singing" (Zephaniah 3:17). He gathers the grieving, saves the lame and gives praise to the disgraced (Zephaniah 3:18, 19). His words are "I will bring you in" (Zephaniah 3:20), and I can tell you those words land softly on somebody who's been left in the dark. So today, baker, trust Him like the humble do, and let yourself be sung over. This is the kind of promise that keeps my ovens warm.
